claims.text: ChatGPT generates hallucinated content by fabricating unverifiable information in approximately 19.5% of user queries.
Existing large language models face significant challenges in recognizing hallucinations in text.
Hallucination recognition in large language models can be improved by providing external knowledge.
Hallucination recognition in large language models can be improved by adding reasoning steps.

evidence.description: Empirical results suggest ChatGPT generates hallucinated content in specific topics by fabricating unverifiable information in about 19.5% of user queries.
Experiments show that existing LLMs face great challenges in recognizing the hallucinations in texts.
Experiments prove that hallucination recognition can be improved by providing external knowledge.
Experiments prove that hallucination recognition can be improved by adding reasoning steps.

methodologies.name: ChatGPT-based sampling-then-filtering framework with human annotation
methodologies.description: A two-step generation framework combined with human labeling to generate and annotate hallucinated samples for evaluating LLM performance.
